stemMd: Which passenger would especially value the new reliability measure?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Someone interested only in the colour of the buses.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Someone whose arrival time has no consequences and who never checks travel information.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Someone comparing only the number of seats.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Someone who must arrive before a fixed interview time.

explanationMd: A fixed interview creates an asymmetric cost: being late can matter much more than being early. Information about unusually long trips helps plan a departure time. This matches the appointment example developed in the passage.

distractorRationale.a: Bus colour is unrelated to journey-time reliability.
distractorRationale.b: The passage’s reasoning concerns decisions affected by timing.
distractorRationale.c: Seat count is not measured by reliability.
distractorRationale.e: No transport decision is affected for this person.
